messages.subject: Matrix - Vector Products etc
parts:
Hi all

Since first taking up TMB, I have been compiling a file of scalar, vector, matrix and array operations building on the cpp file available on the Git Hub. I had recently sent this to Kasper, offering to post these on the hub, soon after which the posts of Jeff and Hans appeared. With Kasper, I have agreed to post these files, and an associated summary text file on the hub, but have been delayed in getting to this. Given the recent posts, here are the files which you may find of assistance. If you have any observations on these, please send then along!

Cheers

Bob

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Matrix - Vector Products etc
parts:
Thanks. This is very useful. Some ideas/questions

1. Should it be merged with matrix_arrays.cpp? (following the principle "do not duplicate information")
2. Is it necessary to  REPORT() following every case? (In my opinion a few examples
    in the beginning of the file is sufficient, and the user will add where required.
   This is easy if the object, e.g. m4_colwise_sum, is allready defined).
3. Are there major areas that are not covered? 
4. Is the information given at http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/Tutorial.html under "Matrices and arrays"
    consistent with your file? Does the tutorial need an update?

messages.author: 5f950c9713997d19
messages.subject: Re: Matrix - Vector Products etc
parts:
Hi Group

Here are some thoughts on this:

1. the file I sent started with the matrix_arrays.cpp file on the hub so what is there should be a subset of the file I sent. I think this file could replace what is now on the hub.
2. Good point. In the existing file, some variables are directly reported e.g REPORT(v1(v1_1)) but I found that this doesn't always work so I took a common approach. It also allowed more descriptive variable names. But as Hans says, a few examples might only be needed.
3. I tried to cover many possible areas of use but this is where a broader set of eyes would help.
4. I think that it is consistent but if not, then certainly change is in order.

Bob

Sounds good. I think your file can replace matrix_arrays.cpp, but most of
the REPORT statements should be left out, with the assumption that the user
will add the ones of interest.

I have created a new branch called "documentation" on github. There we can make changes to the documentation
that later will find its way into TMB. Do you want to fork and pull-request yourself,
or should I do the changes? 

Hans
